subject.title: transcripts: show prints stored terminal escapes from imported text

question: Should this already-public transcript terminal-control injection be handled as a normal public CLI hardening fix, or routed through OpenClaw security handling first?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but untrusted imported text can emit terminal controls through an operator-facing CLI path and the issue carries the protected `security` label.

options.title: Security review then public hardening
options.body: A security reviewer confirms the public handling route, then a focused fix strips terminal controls and adds regression coverage.

options.title: Private security handling
options.body: Pause public repair work and move any fix/backport/advisory decision through the security process despite the report already being public.

recommendation.title: Security review then public hardening
recommendation.body: A security reviewer confirms the public handling route, then a focused fix strips terminal controls and adds regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The core transcript CLI surface history points most strongly to steipete, and this decision needs owner-level judgment on the security handling route.
